identity.title: ALMA 690 GHz Observations of IRAS 16293-2422B: Infall in a Highly Optically Thick Disk

paper_type_evidence.quote: The observations were made with fifteen antennas of ALMA on April 2012, during the ALMA science verification data program.

question.value: What are the continuum structure, line morphology and infall kinematics of IRAS 16293-2422B at 690 GHz, and is its dust optically thick?

evidence.quote: We suggest that the presence of this inner depression and the fact that we do not see inner structure (or a flat structure) in the continuum is produced by very optically thick dust
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00007.SV.
we report $\sim$0.2 arcsec resolution 690 GHz observations obtained with the Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA)

analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate and image continuum and lines

method.value: CASA calibration and CLEAN imaging, robust 0.5

analysis_steps.goal: Brightness temperature and lower-limit dust mass

method.value: Planck-equation Tb from flux and Gaussian beam; optically thin isothermal dust mass

evidence.quote: Assuming that the dust is optically thin and isothermal, the dust mass (M$_d$) will be directly proportional to the flux density

assumptions.value: kappa = 2.2 cm2/g, beta = 0.6, Td = 160 K, d = 120 pc

evidence.quote: as well as a characteristic dust temperature (T$_d$) of 160 K, we estimated a lower limit for the mass for the disk of about 0.03 M$_\odot$

validation.value: Mass uncertainty factor of five from range of opacities in Ossenkopf & Henning

evidence.quote: the level of uncertainty in the mass lower limit is a factor of five

analysis_steps.goal: Moment maps and velocity gradient / dynamical mass

method.value: Moment 0 and 1 maps; Keplerian mass from east-west gradient, corrected by sin(i) with i=5 deg

evidence.quote: If we assume that the rotation is Keplerian and attribute it to a disk in rotation then the dynamical mass associated to this velocity gradient corresponds to only 0.1 M$_\odot$
if we correct by the inclination angle dividing this mass by the $\sin \theta$ with $\theta$ say 5$^\circ$, we obtain a value of 1.2 M$_\odot$

analysis_steps.goal: Fit inverse P-Cygni profiles with two-layer infall model

method.value: Modified two-layer model with fixed Tc=160 K, Phi=0.37, Tx=50 K, Tf=3 K; fit Vin, sigma_v, tau0, VLSR

evidence.quote: The fitting was minimized with a grid search, obtaining the following parameters: $V_{in}$ = 0.7 km s$^{-1}$, $\sigma_v$ = 0.6 km s$^{-1}$, and $\tau_0$ =0.17.
The adopted filling fraction of the continuum source, $\Phi$ =0.37 is consistent with the ratio of solid angles between the region in absorption to the region in emission.

assumptions.value: Tx decreases as sqrt of distance; Pineda gas 50% more distant

evidence.quote: Assuming that the excitation temperature of the molecules decreases as the square root of the distance and that the gas sampled by Pineda et al. (2012) is 50% more distant than that sampled by us, we adopt $T_x$ = 50 K.
The fitting was minimized with a grid search

validation.value: Compared with Pineda et al. 2012 parameters at 220 GHz

evidence.quote: Several of the parameters are quite similar to those derived by Pineda et al. (2012) from lines at 220 GHz.
The data were calibrated, imaged, and analyzed using the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA).
To analyze the data, we also used the KARMA software (cite: Goo1996).

findings_qualitative.value: Line emission forms a ring with central hole around the continuum; cavity to the southeast likely from outflow

evidence.quote: the ring like structure is not completely closed, there is a small cavity towards its southeast

claims.hypothesis: Dust in IRAS 16293-2422B is very optically thick at 690 GHz
claims.experiment: Continuum size and brightness temperature, line hole size
claims.result: Compact 400 mas featureless source, Tb 160 K, line hole comparable to continuum size
claims.finding: Very optically thick dust in innermost region

evidence.quote: produced by very optically thick dust located in the innermost parts of IRAS 16293-2422B

claims.hypothesis: 690 GHz lines trace faster, more turbulent infall closer to the star than 220 GHz
claims.experiment: Two-layer model fit of inverse P-Cygni profiles
claims.result: Vin 0.7 and sigma 0.6 km/s vs ~0.5 and 0.3 for Pineda
claims.finding: Faster, more turbulent gas closer to the central object

evidence.quote: implying that we may be detecting faster, more turbulent gas located closer to the central object

claims.experiment: Moment 1 map velocity gradient and Keplerian mass
claims.result: 1.3 km/s over 60 AU gives 0.1 Msun unless inclination ~5 deg
claims.finding: Disk plane close to plane of the sky

evidence.quote: We therefore conclude that the disk plane of IRAS16293$-$2422B must be located almost on the plane of the sky

why_this_data.value: Lines chosen for good contrast between absorption and emission

evidence.quote: These selected lines show a good contrast between the absorption and emission features as compared with the rest.

limitations_admitted.value: Disk mass is only a lower limit with factor of five uncertainty

evidence.quote: Please note that the level of uncertainty in the mass lower limit is a factor of five
